title: Every index is built without CONCURRENTLY and the migration rewrites scan_history twice inside one transaction, while the self-updater runs it against a still-serving app
description: runPlan wraps the entire plan in a single BEGIN/COMMIT (line 95 to line 134) because "half-migrated schemas are the worst-case outcome", and the file header notes CONCURRENTLY is deliberately avoided since it cannot run in a transaction. The 2.0.0 to 3.0.0 plan contains 18 CREATE TABLE, 48 ADD COLUMN, 17 CREATE INDEX and 18 dataUpdates, all under that one transaction. Two of the ADD COLUMNs force a full rewrite of scan_history and hold ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on it for the whole remaining transaction: `share_token_hash TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` (2.0.0-to-3.0.0.mjs:608-615) and `public_id TEXT DEFAULT (replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', ''))` (line 879-883), whose volatile default is evaluated once per existing row. A third, `UPDATE scan_history SET public_id = ... WHERE public_id IS NULL` (line 1059), is an unbounded UPDATE over the same table. The boot path has the same property without the transaction: all 103 CREATE INDEX / CREATE UNIQUE INDEX statements in instrumentation.ts are plain, taking a SHARE lock that blocks writes for the build, and the same two scan_history rewrites appear at instrumentation.ts:1284 and 2613. The self-updater runs db:migrate from inside the running app and explicitly does not restart it (app/api/v3/admin/updater/apply/route.ts:28), so the app is serving throughout.
impact: At the current production size (roughly 50 users) this is seconds, not minutes, so the practical cost today is a short stall rather than an outage. But every request that reads or writes scan_history or users blocks for the full duration of the migration transaction, with no timeout and no warning anywhere in the UI: the updater dialog tells the operator only that the server is not restarted, implying it keeps serving normally. The cost scales linearly with scan_history, which is the fastest-growing table in the product, so the same release flow gets worse every month with no signal until it is a real outage.
recommendation: Split the plan into a transactional DDL phase and a post-commit index phase, and run the CREATE INDEX steps outside the transaction with CONCURRENTLY (which requires per-statement error handling and a re-run path for INVALID indexes). Set `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` and `statement_timeout` at the start of the migration transaction so a blocked ACCESS EXCLUSIVE acquisition fails fast instead of queuing every request behind it. Add a warning to the updater dialog that db:migrate briefly locks the database.

title: No request or scan correlation id exists anywhere, and system_error_logs stores only a free-text message with no level, route, user, or scan column
description: The only structured error store is system_error_logs, created at instrumentation.ts:636-641 as `(id SERIAL, message TEXT, detail TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ)`. lib/database/error-log-capture.ts:169-173 inserts exactly `(message, detail)`, formed by string-joining whatever arguments a console.error call happened to pass. There is no level column (console.warn is not captured at all, only console.error at :137), no route, no user id, no scan id, and no request id. Nothing in the app generates a request id: no middleware.ts code sets or reads an x-request-id header, and the only `requestId` identifiers in the tree belong to unrelated features (app/api/v3/scan/discover/route.ts:96 for discovery progress, lib/browserbase/network-capture.ts:76 for CDP frames). GET /api/v3/admin/error-logs (app/api/v3/admin/error-logs/route.ts:37) can therefore only offer page/limit/free-text search over message and detail. The gap is visible in the product copy: components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:129 tells the user "The error is logged with the reference below" and no reference is ever rendered, because DashboardErrorState has no id prop at all (:22-33).
impact: When a user reports "my scan failed around 3pm", an operator cannot filter to that user or that scan. They grep free-form English across every console.error the process made, from 328 call sites, with a coalescing window and a 100-insert-per-minute cap (error-log-capture.ts:73-79) that can drop exactly the burst they are looking for. Any multi-hop failure (route -> executeScan -> a check -> safeFetch) produces several unrelated-looking rows with nothing tying them together.
recommendation: Add `level`, `route`, `user_id`, `scan_id` and `request_id` columns to system_error_logs in instrumentation.ts and populate them from an AsyncLocalStorage context set in middleware.ts (generate a request id there, echo it as x-request-id). Have lib/database/error-log-capture.ts read that context in the wrapper at :137. Thread scanId into the scanner's console.error calls. Then surface the id in components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx so the sentence at :129 is true.

title: The nightly cleanup runs about thirty DELETEs, four of them full table scans, inside one 350-line transaction holding a pooled connection
description: `lib/database/cleanup.ts` opens `BEGIN` at line 114 and does not `COMMIT` until line 464, wrapping roughly thirty DELETE statements across sessions, rate_limits, tokens, scan_history, scan_finding_feedback, user_notifications, github_review_usage, ai_conversations and more in a single transaction on one pooled client. Four of those DELETEs cannot use an index and seq-scan their table (see perf-15): rate_limits (line 211), scan_finding_feedback (line 380), user_notifications (line 389), github_review_usage (line 401). None of the work is transactionally coupled -- these are independent retention prunes on unrelated tables.
impact: One of the 10 pool connections is held for the entire pass, and every row deleted stays locked for its duration, so any concurrent write touching those rows blocks. The four full scans make the pass length grow with total table size rather than with the number of rows actually being deleted. A failure at line 480 rolls back thirty prunes that had nothing to do with each other.
recommendation: Split the pass in lib/database/cleanup.ts:114-464 into one autocommitted statement per table (or small groups), with the batching pattern `DELETE ... WHERE ctid IN (SELECT ctid ... LIMIT 5000)` in a loop for the large tables, so no single statement holds locks for long. Add the four missing indexes from perf-15 first.

title: Twelve schema columns are written and never read, or defined and never written
description: Verified dead, each with the grep that found no live reference: users.beta_access (:303) hardcoded false in every INSERT (lib/auth/auth.ts:282,361,382; staff-invite/[token]/route.ts:199), no UPDATE, no gate; users.email_session_revoked (:317) a legacy duplicate whose nine live references all resolve to notification_preferences; users.daily_scan_limit (:304) see drift-05; broadcast_recipients.opened_at and .clicked_at (:1155-1156) DDL only; broadcast_messages.scheduled_at (:1137) inserted but no worker consumes it and status is hardcoded 'draft' then 'sent', so the CHECK values 'scheduled' and 'cancelled' are unwritable; broadcast_messages.message_type (:1135) hardcoded "email" by the UI and never read by the send path (:504); data_requests.completed_at (:876) DDL only, the route uses downloaded_at; system_settings.setting_type (:1121) DDL only; gifted_subscriptions.reason (:950) selected in the GDPR export but the only INSERT (admin/route.ts:1671) omits it and the gift dialog has no field; badges.is_limited (:496) only ever inserted as false with no UPDATE anywhere; api_keys.team_id (:931) no reference in lib/api/api-keys.ts or app/api/v3/keys; scan_screenshots.width and .height (:1381-1382) written at lib/scanner/page-screenshot.ts:295, never selected, consumers read the result_meta copy.
impact: Schema noise that misleads anyone reading the model, plus three cases (beta_access, message_type, scheduled_at) that look like shipped features and are not.
recommendation: Decide per column: wire it or drop it. Deletions need owner sign-off. beta_access, broadcast scheduling and broadcast message_type are the three worth a product decision rather than a silent drop.

title: Webhook HMAC signing secret is stored in plaintext, unlike every other reversible secret in the codebase
description: POST /api/v3/webhooks generates a 256-bit secret and inserts it directly into webhooks.secret, a plain TEXT column. Neither the webhooks route nor lib/webhooks/delivery.ts calls encryptApiKey/decryptApiKey. Every other long-lived secret the app needs back in plaintext for repeated use (API keys, TOTP seeds, Discord OAuth tokens) goes through lib/auth/crypto.ts's AES-256-GCM encryptApiKey/decryptApiKey. A DB-level compromise lets an attacker read every user's webhook secret and forge validly-signed payloads to their receivers.
recommendation: Encrypt webhooks.secret at rest with the existing encryptApiKey/decryptApiKey helpers, decrypting only where signWebhookPayload needs the raw secret. Backfill existing plaintext rows in a migration.

title: Twenty-seven of the ninety-seven indexes are redundant: sixteen duplicate a UNIQUE constraint outright and eleven are strict prefixes of a wider index, and a code comment records the reasoning that created most of them
description: New relative to AUDIT-012#perf-15 and #perf-16, which covered missing and unusable indexes; this is the opposite direction. A UNIQUE constraint is implemented as a unique b-tree index, so a separate CREATE INDEX on the same column is a pure duplicate. Sixteen exist: idx_users_email (:323 vs :284), idx_users_stripe_customer (:326 vs :296), idx_api_keys_key_hash (:373 vs :362), idx_scan_history_share_token (:432 vs :425), idx_badges_name (:499 vs :490), idx_discord_user (:724 vs :711), idx_discord_id (:725 vs :712), idx_notif_prefs_user_id (:830 vs :802), idx_team_invites_token (:916 vs :910), idx_admin_notifications_cookie (:991 vs :966), idx_ai_conversations_session_id (:1192 vs :1184), idx_user_ai_configs_user_id (:1219 vs :1210), idx_github_connections_user (:1932 vs :1924), idx_github_review_usage_user_window (:2047 vs the UNIQUE added at :2034), idx_promoted_auto_tag_rules_tag (:2951 vs :2939), and idx_staff_invites_token (lib/admin/staff-invites.ts:45 vs :37). Eleven more are strict prefixes of a wider index or key, which a b-tree already serves: idx_scan_history_user_id (:430) under idx_scan_history_user_scanned (:1587), idx_api_usage_key_id (:408) under idx_api_usage_key_used (:1589), idx_admin_audit_admin_id (:577) under idx_admin_audit_admin_created (:1591), idx_scan_tags_scan_id (:446) under UNIQUE(scan_id, tag) (:444), idx_user_badges_user (:513) under PRIMARY KEY (user_id, badge_id) (:511), idx_rate_limits_key (:844) under UNIQUE(key, window_start) (:842), idx_device_trust_user_id (:863) under UNIQUE(user_id, device_fingerprint) (:861), idx_team_members_team (:902) under UNIQUE(team_id, user_id) (:900), idx_domains_user_id (:3187) under UNIQUE(user_id, domain) (:3185), idx_api_keys_key_locator_backfill (:376), a partial index whose rows are a subset of idx_api_keys_key_locator (:374), and idx_staff_activity_user_heartbeat (:743), a composite on (user_id, last_heartbeat) on a table with UNIQUE(user_id) (:741), which caps the table at one row per user so the second column can never narrow anything. The comment at :1571-1578 states the reasoning that produced the first three of the prefix cases: "The single-column indexes created above each table are left in place; these are additive, not replacements, so unrelated query shapes that only filter on one of the columns keep working the same way." A composite index leading with the same column already serves a filter on that column alone, so the premise is wrong. Separately, six indexes cover low-cardinality columns on tables that are tiny in this deployment (about 50 users) and will never be chosen by the planner over a sequential scan: idx_users_role (:324), idx_users_plan (:325), idx_admin_notifications_type (:990), idx_access_rules_type (:1023), idx_security_alerts_severity (:1108) and idx_broadcast_messages_status (:1143).
impact: Every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on these tables maintains a second copy of an index that can never be chosen, which is pure write amplification on the hottest tables in the schema: rate_limits (written on every rate-limited request), api_usage, scan_history and sessions. It also inflates the working set that has to stay in shared_buffers and doubles the vacuum work on those relations. The false comment at :1574 is a maintenance hazard on its own, because it will produce more duplicates the next time someone adds a composite index alongside an existing single-column one.
recommendation: Drop the 27 listed indexes with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS`. Keep every UNIQUE constraint, they are the constraints doing the work. Fix the comment at instrumentation.ts:1571-1578 to say that a composite index leading with column A replaces a single-column index on A, and delete the three single-column indexes it was written to justify (:430, :408, :577). Verify against a live database with `SELECT indexrelid::regclass, indrelid::regclass, indkey FROM pg_index ORDER BY indrelid;` before dropping, since a self-hosted install created by an older path may have a slightly different set.

title: REQUIRED_TABLES lists 8 of the 66 tables the app creates and omits sessions, so a boot that fails to create the session table reports a healthy schema while every login 500s
description: REQUIRED_TABLES is `[users, scan_history, api_keys, host_reputation, host_badges, webhooks, scan_finding_feedback, system_error_logs]`. It is consumed by the boot-time verification at instrumentation.ts:3515-3543 (which fires a critical admin alert on a miss) and by GET /api/v3/health at app/api/v3/health/route.ts:110-116 (which reports missing_tables). Cross-checking it against the 64 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements in instrumentation.ts plus the two lazy ones from schema-02: every name in the list is genuinely created, so there is no phantom entry. The gap is the other direction. The file's own docstring says the list covers "auth, scanning, API keys, billing", and `sessions` is absent, even though lib/auth/auth.ts:99 reads it on every authenticated request and losing it takes down login, logout, and every dashboard route. Also absent and load-bearing: `rate_limits` (lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:148, every rate-limited endpoint), `notification_preferences` (inserted on every signup at app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:200 and on every OAuth signup at oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:239), `processed_stripe_events` (the Stripe webhook idempotency guard at app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:168, whose own instrumentation.ts comment at :536-543 documents what happened the last time it was missing: every Stripe retry reprocessed as a new event), and the three payment idempotency ledgers ai_credit_purchases, github_credit_purchases and browserbase_credit_purchases, each of which is the sole guard against double-crediting a purchase (lib/billing/ai-usage.ts:160-172). Every one of those tables is created inside a `.catch()` that only console.errors, exactly the failure mode this list exists to catch.
impact: The health endpoint is the operator's only signal that the boot-time schema sequence half-completed. Today it can report schema_ok with no missing tables while sessions, rate_limits or processed_stripe_events do not exist, which means a monitor watching /api/v3/health stays green through an outage that makes login impossible or through a state where every Stripe webhook replay re-grants a plan.
recommendation: Add sessions, rate_limits, notification_preferences, processed_stripe_events, ai_credit_purchases, github_credit_purchases and browserbase_credit_purchases to REQUIRED_TABLES, plus staff_invites and admin_audit_log_archive once schema-02 is fixed. The docstring's argument against exhaustiveness (drift with instrumentation.ts) holds for a full 66-name list but not for the seven tables whose absence takes down auth, rate limiting, signup or billing idempotency.

title: Column types are inconsistent for the same kind of value across tables: IP addresses in three different types, and two JSON payloads stored as TEXT
description: The schema stores an IP address three different ways: `INET` in security_alerts.ip_address (instrumentation.ts:1100), `VARCHAR(45)` in sessions (:336), sessions.ipv4_address (:352), api_keys.bound_ip (:382), admin_audit_log (:574), device_trust (:856) and access_rules (implicitly, in the TEXT `value` column at :1009), and plain `TEXT` in staff_activity.ip_address (:736). Only the INET column can be compared with a subnet operator or validated by the database; the VARCHAR ones silently accept anything up to 45 characters, which matters for api_keys.bound_ip because lib/api/api-keys.ts's passesApiKeyIpBinding compares it as a string. Two JSON payloads are stored as TEXT while everything else in the schema uses JSONB: `users.backup_codes TEXT` (:316), which is written with JSON.stringify (app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:110) and read with JSON.parse (:49), and which app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:156 probes with the string comparison `u.backup_codes IS NOT NULL AND u.backup_codes != '[]'` to compute has_backup_codes, so any serialization that emits `[ ]` or `null` instead of exactly `[]` flips that flag; and `data_requests.data TEXT` (:874), which holds the whole GDPR export document. Positives worth recording, since they are the things that usually go wrong: money is integer cents everywhere (billing_history.amount_cents INTEGER at :525, all three credit ledgers use BIGINT token counts), there is no float anywhere in the schema, and every timestamp is TIMESTAMPTZ or TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE with no naked `timestamp` column, so there is no time-zone ambiguity to fix.
impact: No current failure. The cost is that a query cannot mix these columns (you cannot join or compare security_alerts.ip_address against sessions.ip_address without a cast), no CIDR or subnet analysis is possible over the VARCHAR ones, and the has_backup_codes flag in the admin user detail view depends on exact string equality with '[]' rather than on a structural check the database could do.
recommendation: Low priority, but when any of these tables is next touched: migrate staff_activity.ip_address to VARCHAR(45) to match its six siblings (or migrate all seven to INET, which is the better target and lets the admin panel do subnet queries), and convert users.backup_codes and data_requests.data to JSONB so app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:156 can use `jsonb_array_length(backup_codes) > 0` instead of comparing text to '[]'. Both conversions are `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE jsonb USING col::jsonb`, safe on existing rows since both already contain valid JSON.
